evidence_basis: Body text read for abstract, introduction, results 2.1 and 2.5, discussion and methods; figure images were not seen and not every results subsection was read line by line (2.2-2.4 were keyword-scanned).

Locator L1 (Abstract; for: Triac rescues myelination and PV+ interneuron maturation in Mct8/Oatp1c1 Dko mice only with early postnatal treatment): "Triac treatment (400 ng/g) induced normalized myelination, cortical GABAergic interneuron differentiation, electrophysiological parameters, and locomotor performance only when administered during the first three postnatal weeks."

Locator L2 (Results 2.5; for: Late window: myelination not improved): "In contrast, in Dko mice that received Triac only between postnatal week 3 and 6, myelination was not improved while a partial recovery of PV+ immunoreactivity could still be detected."

Locator L3 (Discussion; for: High-dose Triac in mice: peripheral thyrotoxic state): "Triac is most likely the only TH receptor active substance in these animals with such a high thyromimetic activity (at the highest dose) that it still causes a peripheral thyrotoxic state as indicated by the elevated hepatic and renal Dio1 expression"

Locator L4 (Discussion; for: Thyroid axis suppression at the effective dose): "The high concentration of Triac needed for effective normalization of brain parameters in our mouse model resulted in a fully downregulated HPT axis with Tshb transcript below the detection limit"

Locator L5 (Discussion; for: Low dose (clinical-range per the authors) ineffective on brain readouts in the mouse): "treating Dko mice with such a low Triac dose had only little beneficial effects on brain parameters such as myelination or interneuron maturation"

Locator L6 (Discussion; for: Triac CNS entry route not identified in this paper): "As one hypothesis, the not-yet identified transport systems by which Triac enters the CNS and neural target cells might be down-regulated in the mature mouse CNS"
